classification.difficultyReason: Select the correct zero and read a dual-scale protractor for acute and obtuse angles.

content.prompt: Read the angle $AOB$ that is being measured by the protractor in each of these diagrams.

spec.description: Editable semicircular protractor with both opposite degree scales, every one-degree tick, ten-degree numerals, rectangular base, centre O, rightward OA and upward-right OB. Ordinary source blue strokes become house black.
spec.mathematics: OA lies at the right-hand zero. OB intersects the inner scale at 52 and the outer scale at 128; only the source's ten-degree numerals are printed. The marked sector is acute.
spec.answerVisibility: The protractor and rays are permanent givens; no numerical answer is added to the student figure.

answer.worked: Start at the right-hand $0^\circ$, along $OA$, and read the inner scale where $OB$ crosses it. Thus $\angle AOB=52^\circ$.

spec.description: Editable semicircular protractor with both opposite degree scales, every one-degree tick, ten-degree numerals, rectangular base, centre O, leftward OA and upward-right OB. Ordinary source blue strokes become house black.
spec.mathematics: OA lies at the left-hand zero. OB intersects the outer scale at 122 and the inner scale at 58; only the source's ten-degree numerals are printed. The marked sector is obtuse.
spec.answerVisibility: The protractor and rays are permanent givens; no numerical answer is added to the student figure.

answer.worked: Start at the left-hand $0^\circ$, along $OA$, and read the outer scale where $OB$ crosses it. Thus $\angle AOB=122^\circ$, an obtuse angle.
